Brand mark / Disruption Now The mark is one locked unit.
The Disruption Now wordmark with the purple brush Now, here in white on charcoal. The wordmark and the Now are one mark, never separated. The seven properties below are locked on every file.
The mark
What the mark is. Seven properties, all locked.
The Disruption Now lockup is the wordmark plus the brush Now. These seven properties define it and do not change between files.
DISRUPTION face

Now face

Now position

What the MidwestCon mark means
The mark is a plug, built from skin tones, in three pillars.
The MidwestCon mark is a plug. The conference is where people plug in, connect, and draw power from one another. It is drawn in three skin tones because the work is people-first, and each bar names one of the three worlds MidwestCon brings together. Pick a pillar to read what it carries; its label and its bar light up on the mark.
01 · Top bar · lightest tone
Artistic Intelligence
Artistic Intelligence is the create side of MidwestCon. Artists, designers, and builders who make images, music, and stories with these tools. The conference reads the letters as artistic, not only artificial, and gives that work its own stage.
02 · Middle bar · mid tone
Policy Innovation
Policy Innovation is the govern side. Lawmakers, regulators, and the policy and compliance leads inside companies, working on rules that keep up with the technology. MidwestCon brings them together with the people building it, so both groups shape AI in the same week.
03 · Bottom bar · deepest tone
Tech for social impact
Tech for social impact is the build and fund side pointed at the public good. Founders and funders building AI for the small business, the school, and the public-sector team, the people the tech industry usually serves last. It is the Disruption Now mission made concrete.
Why a plug, in skin tones. The prongs and the cord make the connector literal. MidwestCon is where these three worlds plug into each other and draw power. The three bars run light to deep in skin tones because the mark is built out of the people MidwestCon gathers, not an abstract symbol. The MIDWESTCON wordmark carries the same gradient. The tone order is the stack of the plug, not a ranking.
Backgrounds
Which version goes on which background.
Every logo has a version built to read on dark and a version built to read on light. Pick the one that has contrast.
White lockups go on dark
The white Disruption Now lockup and the white MidwestCon wordmark go on charcoal, photos, and dark color fields.
Dark lockups go on light
The dark versions go on white and light backgrounds, where the near-black wordmark stays sharp.
Square marks for square slots
The square Disruption Now monogram and the square MidwestCon lockup fit profile photos, app icons, and any square space.
The icon alone when space is tight
Use the MidwestCon icon by itself for favicons and small stamps where the full name would not read.
Clear space
Clear space.
Keep a margin of empty space around the mark so it reads as the anchor on the surface. The rule is half the cap-height of DISRUPTION on all four sides. The diagram is the real mark, measured.
Keep the margin clear
Type, photos, cards, and bright accents all stay outside the dashed boundary. The lockup needs the space to read.
Minimum size
Minimum size.
Stop shrinking the lockup before the brush Now stops reading. Below that floor, switch to the monogram or the icon, which are built for small spaces. These widths are a starting point; the exact floor is still being finalized.
About 220 px wide is a sensible floor for the horizontal lockup on screen. The Now still reads.
Smaller than that, switch to the square monogram or the MidwestCon icon. A shrunken wordmark stops reading.
Co-branding
Co-branding. How a partner mark sits with ours.
When a partner or sub-brand mark shares a surface with Disruption Now, the Disruption Now mark leads and the partner mark stays subordinate. These four rules set the size and the placement. The five named combinations and when to use each live on the brand-mark combinations page.
Hierarchy
The Disruption Now mark leads. A partner or sub-brand mark sits smaller and stays subordinate, sized to sit next to the Disruption Now mark without competing with it. Each partner mark has a different shape, so set the size per surface. Worked example: on a Rob Richardson speaker card, the MidwestCon mark sits at 32% of the title block with its by Disruption Now line intact.
Sequence
Disruption Now reads first, the partner mark follows in reading order. Put the partner first only when that piece is about the partner.
Distance
Place the two marks as far apart as the layout allows, often opposite corners, so the hierarchy reads at a glance. Keep clear space around each one. Pull them closer only when the point is the relationship between them.
Alignment
Line the two marks up on a shared horizontal or vertical edge. A partner mark that is shorter than the Disruption Now mark can center on its height.
More than two marks.
Partner row on a cover
Several partner logos sit evenly spaced across the bottom of the slide, each in its own colors, on a flat photo or a charcoal-bordered card. The cover signature for a multi-partner proposal.
Logo wall (trusted by, past sponsors)
A grid of partner logos in their authentic colors, at least 40 px apart, on a light-grey or depth-purple card. Use light-grey when the logos are full-color, depth-purple when they are white on transparent.
The five named ways the marks combine, and which to use on which surface, live at how the brand marks combine. Big Kitty Labs is credited as the build partner, not co-branded as an equal; the partner directory is at build partners.
Social icons
Platform icons stay in their own colors.
On a social-icon row, each platform keeps its own brand color. Do not recolor them to Disruption Now purple. Size them 48 to 56 px tall.

Don'ts
What never to do.
Seven edits that break the mark. Keep the file as it goes out.
Do not recolor the marks
Keep the purple Now, the MidwestCon skin-tone gradient, and any partner mark in their own colors. Recoloring a partner mark also breaks its trademark terms.
Do not let a partner mark outsize Disruption Now
The Disruption Now mark leads on a co-branded surface. A partner or sub-brand mark stays smaller, unless the piece is about the partner.
Do not separate the Now from DISRUPTION
The wordmark and the brush Now are one mark. DISRUPTION on its own is not the Disruption Now logo.
Do not rotate the brush Now
The Now sits level in the lockup. Rotation is reserved for in-headline emphasis, never the logo.
Do not stretch or squeeze
Scale the file evenly so the proportions hold. Hold Shift, or set width and height to the same percentage.
Do not add effects
No shadows, glows, or outlines on the logo. The mark carries itself.
Do not put a logo on a background that hides it
A white lockup needs a dark surface. A dark lockup needs a light one. Pick the version that has contrast.
